prompt: CHALLENGE: Target: 2-methyl-2-butanol. You have ONLY methylmagnesium bromide (CH₃MgBr) available as the organometallic. From which carbonyl precursor can you build the target?

options.label: 2-butanone (CH₃COCH₂CH₃) + CH₃MgBr → 2-methyl-2-butanol. The ethyl group comes 'free' from the ketone side.
Acetone + CH₃MgBr gives 2-methyl-2-propanol (tert-butanol), not the target.
Methyl propanoate + CH₃MgBr — gives 2-methyl-2-butanol only via DOUBLE addition of CH₃ (6 carbons wouldn't fit).

explanation: Retrosynthesis gives you three C–C disconnections on a tertiary alcohol. Only two require ethyl Grignard (which you lack). The 'add methyl to 2-butanone' disconnect uses just CH₃MgBr. Learning to see which bond you CAN disconnect given reagent limits is the heart of synthesis.
